L2@P0-1: SUMMARY OF PRODUCT CHARACTERISTICS2
L3@P1: © ESTEVE (2025) CONFIDENTIAL
L4@P1: 1. NAME OF THE MEDICINAL PRODUCT
L5@P1: MEPACT 4 mg powder for concentrate for dispersion for infusion
L6@P1: 2. QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE COMPOSITION
L7@P1: Each vial contains 4 mg mifamurtide*.
L8@P1: After reconstitution, each mL of suspension in the vial contains 0.08 mg mifamurtide.
L9@P1: *fully synthetic analogue of a component of Mycobacterium sp. cell wall.
L10@P1: For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.
L11@P1: 3. PHARMACEUTICAL FORM
L12@P1: Powder for concentrate for dispersion for infusion
L13@P1: White to off-white homogeneous cake or powder.
L14@P1: 4. CLINICAL PARTICULARS
L15@P1: 4.1 Therapeutic indications
L16@P1: MEPACT is indicated in children, adolescents and young adults for the treatment of high-grade
L17@P1: resectable non-metastatic osteosarcoma after macroscopically complete surgical resection. It is
L18@P1: used in combination with post-operative multi-agent chemotherapy. Safety and efficacy have been
L19@P1: assessed in studies of patients 2 to 30 years of age at initial diagnosis (see section 5.1).
L20@P1: 4.2 Posology and method of administration
L21@P1: Mifamurtide treatment should be initiated and supervised by specialist physicians experienced in
L22@P1: the diagnosis and treatment of osteosarcoma.
L23@P1: Posology
L24@P1: The recommended dose of mifamurtide for all patients is 2 mg/m2 body surface area. It should be
L25@P1: administered as adjuvant therapy following resection: twice weekly at least 3 days apart for
L26@P1: 12 weeks, followed by once-weekly treatments for an additional 24 weeks for a total of
L27@P1: 48 infusions in 36 weeks.
L28@P1: Special populations
L29@P1: Adults > 30 years
L30@P1: None of the patients treated in the osteosarcoma studies were 65 years or older and in the phase III
L31@P1: randomised study, only patients up to the age of 30 years were included. Therefore, there are not
L32@P1: sufficient data to recommend the use of MEPACT in patients > 30 years of age.
L33@P1: Renal or hepatic impairment
L34@P1: There are no clinically meaningful effects of mild to moderate renal (creatinine clearance
L35@P1: (CrCL) ≥ 30 mL/min) or hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A or B) on the pharmacokinetics of
L36@P1: mifamurtide; therefore, dose adjustments are not necessary for these patients. However, as the
L37@P1: variability in pharmacokinetics of mifamurtide is greater in subjects with moderate hepatic impairment
L38@P1: (see section 5.2), and safety data in patients with moderate hepatic impairment is limited, caution
L39@P1-2: when administering mifamurtide to patients with moderate hepatic impairment is recommended. 3
L40@P2: © ESTEVE (2025) CONFIDENTIAL
L41@P2: As no pharmacokinetic data of mifamurtide is available in patients with severe renal or hepatic
L42@P2: impairment, caution when administering mifamurtide to these patients is recommended. Continued
L43@P2: monitoring of the kidney and liver function is recommended if mifamurtide is used beyond
L44@P2: completion of chemotherapy until all therapy is completed.
L45@P2: Paediatric population < 2 years
L46@P2: The safety and efficacy of mifamurtide in children aged 0 to 2 years have not been established. No
L47@P2: data are available.
L48@P2: Method of administration
L49@P2: MEPACT is administered by intravenous infusion over a period of 1 hour.
L50@P2: MEPACT must not be administered as a bolus injection.
L51@P2: For further instructions on reconstitution, filtering using the filter provided and dilution of the
L52@P2: medicinal product before administration, see section 6.6.
L53@P2: 4.3 Contraindications
L54@P2: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
L55@P2: Concurrent use with ciclosporin or other calcineurin inhibitors (see section 4.5).
L56@P2: Concurrent use with high-dose non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs, cyclooxygenase
L57@P2: inhibitors) (see section 4.5).
L58@P2: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use
L59@P2: Respiratory distress
L60@P2: In patients with a history of asthma or other chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, consideration
L61@P2: should be given to administration of bronchodilators on a prophylactic basis. Two patients with
L62@P2: pre-existing asthma developed mild to moderate respiratory distress associated with the treatment
L63@P2: (see section 4.8). If a severe respiratory reaction occurs, administration of mifamurtide should be
L64@P2: discontinued and appropriate treatment initiated.
L65@P2: Neutropenia
L66@P2: Administration of mifamurtide was commonly associated with transient neutropenia, usually when
L67@P2: used in conjunction with chemotherapy. Episodes of neutropenic fever should be monitored and
L68@P2: managed appropriately. Mifamurtide may be given during periods of neutropenia, but subsequent
L69@P2: fever attributed to the treatment should be monitored closely. Fever or chills persisting for more
L70@P2: than 8 hours after administration of mifamurtide should be evaluated for possible sepsis.
L71@P2: Inflammatory response
L72@P2: Association of mifamurtide with signs of pronounced inflammatory response, including
L73@P2: pericarditis and pleuritis, was uncommon. It should be used with caution in patients with a history
L74@P2: of autoimmune, inflammatory or other collagen diseases. During mifamurtide administration,
L75@P2: patients should be monitored for unusual signs or symptoms, such as arthritis or synovitis,
L76@P2: suggestive of uncontrolled inflammatory reactions.
L77@P2: Cardiovascular disorders
L78@P2: Patients with a history of venous thrombosis, vasculitis or unstable cardiovascular disorders
L79@P2-3: should be closely monitored during mifamurtide administration. If symptoms are persistent and 4
L80@P3: © ESTEVE (2025) CONFIDENTIAL
L81@P3: worsening, administration should be delayed or discontinued. Haemorrhage was observed in
L82@P3: animals at very high doses. These are not expected at the recommended dose, however monitoring
L83@P3: of clotting parameters after the first dose and once again after several doses is recommended.
L84@P3: Allergic reactions
L85@P3: Occasional allergic reactions have been associated with mifamurtide treatment, including rash,
L86@P3: shortness of breath and grade 4 hypertension (see section 4.8). It may be difficult to distinguish
L87@P3: allergic reactions from exaggerated inflammatory responses, but patients should be monitored for
L88@P3: signs of allergic reactions.
L89@P3: Gastrointestinal toxicity
L90@P3: Nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite are very common adverse reactions to mifamurtide (see
L91@P3: section 4.8). Gastrointestinal toxicity may be exacerbated when mifamurtide is used in
L92@P3: combination with high dose, multi-agent chemotherapy and was associated with an increased use
L93@P3: of parenteral nutrition.
L94@P3: MEPACT contains sodium
L95@P3: This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per dosage unit.
L96@P3: 4.5 Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction
L97@P3: Limited studies of the interaction of mifamurtide with chemotherapy have been conducted.
L98@P3: Although these studies are not conclusive, there is no evidence of interference of mifamurtide with
L99@P3: the anti-tumour effects of chemotherapy and vice versa.
L100@P3: It is recommended to separate the administration times of mifamurtide and doxorubicin or other
L101@P3: lipophilic medicinal products if used in the same chemotherapy regimen.
L102@P3: The use of mifamurtide concurrently with ciclosporin or other calcineurin inhibitors is
L103@P3: contraindicated due to their hypothesised effect on splenic macrophages and mononuclear
L104@P3: phagocytic function (see section 4.3).
L105@P3: Also, it has been demonstrated in vitro that high-dose NSAIDs (cyclooxygenase inhibitors) can
L106@P3: block the macrophage activating effect of liposomal mifamurtide. Therefore, the use of high-dose
L107@P3: NSAIDs is contraindicated (see section 4.3).
L108@P3: Because mifamurtide acts through stimulation of the immune system, the chronic or routine use of
L109@P3: corticosteroids should be avoided during treatment with mifamurtide.
L110@P3: In vitro interaction studies showed that liposomal and non-liposomal mifamurtide do not inhibit
L111@P3: the metabolic activity of cytochrome P450 in pooled human liver microsomes. Liposomal and
L112@P3: non-liposomal mifamurtide do not induce the metabolic activity or the transcription of cytochrome
L113@P3: P450 in primary cultures of freshly isolated human hepatocytes. Mifamurtide is, therefore, not
L114@P3: expected to interact with the metabolism of substances that are hepatic cytochrome P450
L115@P3: substrates.
L116@P3: In a large controlled randomised study, mifamurtide used at the recommended dose and schedule
L117@P3: with other medicinal products that have known renal (cisplatin, ifosfamide) or hepatic (high-dose
L118@P3: methotrexate, ifosfamide) toxicities did not exacerbate those toxicities and there was no need to
L119@P3-4: adjust mifamurtide dose.5
L120@P4: © ESTEVE (2025) CONFIDENTIAL
L121@P4: 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation
L122@P4: Pregnancy
L123@P4: There are no data from the use of mifamurtide in pregnant women. Animal studies are insufficient
L124@P4: with respect to reproductive toxicity (see section 5.3). Mifamurtide is not recommended for use during
L125@P4: pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential not using effective contraception.
L126@P4: Breast-feeding
L127@P4: It is unknown whether mifamurtide is excreted in human milk. The excretion of mifamurtide in
L128@P4: milk has not been studied in animals. A decision on whether to continue/discontinue
L129@P4: breast-feeding or to continue/discontinue therapy should be made taking into account the benefit
L130@P4: of breast-feeding to the child and the benefit of mifamurtide therapy to the woman.
L131@P4: Fertility
L132@P4: No dedicated fertility studies have been conducted with mifamurtide (see section 5.3).
L133@P4: 4.7 Effects on ability to drive and use machines
L134@P4: MEPACT has a moderate influence on the ability to drive and use machines. Dizziness, vertigo,
L135@P4: fatigue and blurred vision have shown as very common or common undesirable effects of
L136@P4: mifamurtide treatment.
L137@P4: 4.8 Undesirable effects
L138@P4: Summary of the safety profile
L139@P4: Mifamurtide was studied as a single agent in 248 patients with mostly advanced malignancies during
L140@P4: the early, single arm phase I and II clinical studies. The most frequent adverse reactions are chills,
L141@P4: pyrexia, fatigue, nausea, tachycardia and headache. Many of the very commonly reported adverse
L142@P4: reactions as shown in the following summary table are thought to be related to the mechanism of
L143@P4: action of mifamurtide (see table 1). The majority of these events were reported as either mild or
L144@P4: moderate.
L145@P4: Tabulated list of adverse reactions
L146@P4: Adverse reactions are classified according to system organ class and frequency. Frequency
L147@P4: groupings are defined according to the following convention: very common (≥ 1/10), common
L148@P4: (≥ 1/100 to < 1/10), not known (cannot be estimated from the available data). Within each
L149@P4: frequency grouping, adverse reactions are presented in order of decreasing seriousness.
